name: neurocranium
definition: Anatomical cluster that is the regional skeletal system surrounding the brain.

spatial.dv: dorsal half of the head, floor and walls around the brain, above the pharynx
spatial.landmarks: from the ethmoid plate at the snout to the occipital arch at the first vertebra; roofs the orbit and otic capsule

shape.notes: Model a shallow trough (lathe or extruded U-profile) under the brain. Paired trabeculae (thin rods) fuse anteriorly into a flat ethmoid plate. Parachordals flank the notochord tip posteriorly. Add a dermal roof (frontal, parietal) only from the juvenile stage.

sizes.note: trabeculae plus ethmoid plate; scaled to a 3.1 mm embryo
cartilaginous neurocranium of a 3.9 mm larva
skull of a 28 mm SL adult; head length about 0.25 SL

events.event: trabeculae cranii are the first neurocranial cartilage (ZFIN start stage High-pec)
parachordal cartilages and the ethmoid plate appear (ZFIN start stage Long-pec)
occipital arch cartilages fuse and meet medially as the tectum synoticum by 12 dpf
frontal bone ossifies (ZFIN start stage Days 21-29)
ethmoid cartilage is replaced by bone (ZFIN end stage Days 30-44 for the cartilage)

visibleFromNote: ZFIN gives start stage Unknown. The first Alcian-positive element, the trabecula cranii, has ZFIN start stage High-pec (42 hpf).
notes: Group node. Sub-elements with their own ZFA ids: trabecula cranii ZFA:0001507, ethmoid cartilage ZFA:0001405, parachordal cartilage ZFA:0001423, parasphenoid ZFA:0000561, frontal bone ZFA:0000514, parietal bone ZFA:0000486.

name: splanchnocranium
definition: Anatomical cluster that is the regional skeletal system of the jaws, hyoid and branchial arches.

spatial.dv: ventral half of the head, below the neurocranium and eye, around the pharynx
spatial.landmarks: from the mouth (anterior tip of Meckel's cartilage) to the last gill arch under the otic capsule

shape.notes: Group of seven bilateral arches. Model each arch as one or two bent tubes (dorsal and ventral elements) hanging from the neurocranium and meeting at the ventral midline.

sizes.note: first condensations; arch 1 and 2 elements distinct by 55 hpf
all seven arches cartilaginous in a 3.9 mm larva
jaws plus opercular series of a 28 mm SL adult

events.event: ZFIN start stage 10-13 somites (arch primordia)
cartilage pattern of the pharyngeal arches emerges between 45 and 72 hpf
Meckel's cartilage, palatoquadrate and ceratohyal are distinct cartilage elements by 55 hpf
opercle is the first dermal bone of the arch skeleton to mineralize (3 dpf)
larvae start feeding at 4 dpf with a functional jaw

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage is 10-13 somites (14 hpf) for the arch primordia. Alcian-positive cartilage is present from about 48 to 55 hpf.
notes: Group node for the pharyngeal skeleton. Children in this file: Meckel's cartilage, palatoquadrate, ceratohyal, hyosymplectic, pharyngeal arch 3-7 skeleton, ceratobranchial 5 tooth, dentary, maxilla, opercle.

name: Meckel's cartilage
definition: Meckel's cartilage is the bilaterally paired, rod-like, cartilaginous ventral component of the lower jaw, or ventral mandibular arch. It is typically resorbed in adults.

spatial.dv: ventral-most element of the head, floor of the mouth
spatial.landmarks: left and right rods meet at the anterior midline (mandibular symphysis); posterior end articulates with the palatoquadrate

shape.notes: Two curved rods forming a V that opens posteriorly. Diameter about 1 to 2 chondrocytes (15 to 25 um) in the larva. Later wrap in a thin dentary bone shell.

sizes.note: condensation becoming a distinct rod by 55 hpf
rod that spans the mediolateral width with single stacked chondrocytes; length is an estimate
lower jaw of a 28 mm SL adult, largely replaced by dentary and anguloarticular bone

events.event: mesenchymal precartilage condensation in the mandibular arch at the start of the hatching period
Meckel's cartilage is present and distinct from the palatoquadrate by 55 hpf
dentary osteoblasts appear along the anterolateral surface at 78 hpf
chondrocytes span the mediolateral width; growth by cell intercalation

name: palatoquadrate cartilage
definition: Cartilage that is the dorsal component of the first pharyngeal arch.  It is roughly triangular with slightly concave dorsal edges and convex ventral edges.  The anteroventral corner gives rise the quadrate and articulates with the posterior end of  Meckel's cartilage.  The anterodorsal tip articulates with the lateral edge of the ethmoid plate and the posteroventral edge articulates with the anterodorsal edge of the hyosymplectic.

spatial.dv: lateral to the pharynx, between Meckel's cartilage below and the ethmoid plate above
spatial.landmarks: anteroventral corner (quadrate) meets Meckel's cartilage; anterodorsal tip meets the ethmoid plate; posterior edge meets the hyosymplectic

shape.notes: Roughly triangular flat plate (thickness one chondrocyte) with a longer horizontal ventral edge. Orient in a parasagittal plane, tilted so its dorsal tip leans medially.

sizes.note: quadrate, autopalatine, ectopterygoid and entopterygoid bones replace it in the adult

events.event: distinct element by 55 hpf
cartilage pattern of the mandibular arch complete by 72 hpf
quadrate ossification in the perichondrium (unverified timing)

name: ceratohyal cartilage
definition: Pharyngeal arch cartilage that is bilaterally paired and the largest cartilaginous component of the ventral hyoid arch.

spatial.dv: ventral head, behind and below Meckel's cartilage, floor of the pharynx
spatial.landmarks: left and right rods form an inverted V that points anteriorly; posterior ends meet the hyosymplectic below the ear

shape.notes: Straight rod, thicker at the posterior end (dumbbell from 150 hpf). Angle between left and right rods about 60 to 90 degrees in the larva (the classic ceratohyal angle metric).

sizes.note: multilayer condensation at 55 hpf
dumbbell shape at 150 hpf; length is an estimate

events.event: condensation of chondrogenic cells in several layers by 55 hpf
straightened rod by 79 hpf
ceratohyal bone appears in the perichondrium at 150 hpf
four perichondral bones almost cover the cartilage by 516 hpf

name: hyosymplectic cartilage
definition: Bilaterally paired large cartilage that articulates with the chondrocranium dorsally, the opercle posteriorly, and the palatoquadrate cartilage anteriorly.

spatial.dv: lateral head wall below the otic capsule, above the ceratohyal
spatial.landmarks: dorsal end hangs from the otic region of the neurocranium; posterior edge carries the opercle joint; anteroventral symplectic process reaches the palatoquadrate

shape.notes: Flat plate with a ventral rod (symplectic). Model as a vertical plate about one chondrocyte thick with a tapered ventral spur.

sizes.note: dorsal chondrification site of the hyoid condensation
hyomandibula and symplectic bones

events.event: hyoid condensation splits into a dorsal hyosymplectic and a ventral ceratohyal site
opercle articulates with the hyosymplectic by a ball-and-socket joint from 3 dpf

name: pharyngeal arch 3-7 skeleton
definition: Skeletal and cartilaginous elements of the gill arches; the last five of the set of seven pharyngeal arches; the numbering system can be confusing; generally branchial arch #1 is the first gill arch, or the third pharyngeal arch, but some authors do not follow this convention.

spatial.dv: ventrolateral head, floor and sides of the pharynx behind the ceratohyal
spatial.landmarks: five bilateral gill arches (ceratobranchials 1-5) stacked anteroposteriorly under the otic capsule; ceratobranchial 5 carries the teeth

shape.notes: Array of five bent rods per side (ceratobranchials). Each is about 60 to 70 percent of the ceratohyal length in the larva. The rods converge on a midline copula. Add short dorsal epibranchials as second rods.

sizes.note: ceratobranchial 1 and 5 first (ZFIN start Long-pec)
all five ceratobranchials cartilaginous

events.event: ceratobranchial 1 and 5 cartilages appear (ZFIN start Long-pec)
ceratobranchials 2 to 4 appear (ZFIN start Pec-fin)
gill filament buds form on the four gill-bearing arches late in the hatching period
ceratobranchial 1 to 4 bones ossify (ZFIN start Days 14-20)

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage is 10-13 somites (14 hpf) for the arch skeleton primordia. Cartilage rods are visible from 48 to 60 hpf.

name: ceratobranchial 5 tooth
definition: Is a multi-tissue structure composed of dentine, enameloid and tooth pulp. The tips of the ceratobranchial 5 teeth form before the ceratobranchial itself (3.0 mm NL). As they grow ventrally, they meet the perichondrally ossified surface of ceratobranchial 5 and become firmly ankylosed to the bone. Ceratobranchial teeth are the only teeth present in zebrafish and other cypriniforms.

spatial.dv: floor of the posterior pharynx, medial face of ceratobranchial 5
spatial.landmarks: one ventral row of up to 5 teeth plus two dorsal rows per side in the adult; the only teeth in zebrafish

shape.notes: Tiny cones (10 to 20 um at 48 hpf, about 300 um in adults) pointing dorsomedially from ceratobranchial 5. Render as a cluster of cones; count grows with stage.

sizes.note: tooth tips form before the ceratobranchial itself (3.0 mm NL)
6 teeth at day 5
11 tooth positions per side in three rows; count and size unverified

events.event: tooth tips form at 3.0 mm NL, before ceratobranchial 5 ossifies
6 teeth (day 5)
8 teeth (days 7-13)
10 teeth (days 14-20)
12 teeth (days 45-89)

name: dentary
definition: Dermal bone that forms the antero-lateral part of the lower jaw. It first appears around the anterior end of Meckel's cartilage (5.1 mm NL). In the adult, the dentary meets its counterpart anteriorly at the mandibular symphysis. The dentary abuts the retroarticular posteriorly, and it surround the anguloarticular. The dentary is connected to the maxilla by the maxillo-mandibular ligament. Dentary teeth are absent in cypriniforms, but are present in other ostariophysans.

spatial.dv: ventral-most bone of the head, lateral to the anterior half of Meckel's cartilage
spatial.landmarks: meets its partner at the mandibular symphysis; forms the outer surface of the lower jaw

shape.notes: Thin bony sleeve wrapped around the anterior half of Meckel's cartilage. Start as a short splint, then extend to a plate that covers the cartilage.

sizes.note: single Alizarin-red splint at 86 to 96 hpf

events.event: dentary osteoblasts appear along Meckel's cartilage at 78 hpf
Alizarin red staining of the dentary at 86 hpf
Cubbage and Mabee report the dentary first at 5.1 mm NL (cited in the ZFA definition); timing differs between rearing conditions

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage Unknown. FishFace reports Alizarin-red-positive dentary at 86 hpf; the ZFA definition (from Cubbage and Mabee 1996) gives 5.1 mm NL.

name: maxilla
definition: The dermal maxilla forms part of the upper jaw. It is first visible as a small dorsoventrally oriented rod of bone in the lateral region of the upper jaw. Through anterior ossification it becomes S-shaped, with its anteriormost tip directed medially (4.8 mm NL). The posteroventral end of the maxilla is connected to the dentary by a ligament. Maxillary teeth are absent in cypriniforms, but are present in other ostariophysans. Two barbels are present on the maxilla. The presence of two pairs of maxillary barbels is considered by Cavender and Coburn (1992) to be the primitive condition for the Cyprinidae.

spatial.dv: upper lip region, lateral to the mouth, below the eye
spatial.landmarks: dorsoventral rod at the corner of the mouth; premaxilla lies anterior to its dorsal tip; maxillary barbel attaches to its posteroventral end

shape.notes: Thin S-shaped rod oriented dorsoventrally; the anterior tip turns medially. Pair with a small L-shaped premaxilla (ZFA:0000567) anteriorly.

sizes.note: first visible at 4.8 mm NL

events.event: first visible as a small dorsoventral rod at 4.8 mm NL (about 4.5 mm TL is reached at days 7-13)
premaxilla appears anterior to the maxilla at 5.7 mm
maxillary barbel bud forms at the posteroventral corner at 30 to 40 dpf

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage Unknown. The ZFA definition gives 4.8 mm NL, which the ZFIN stage table places in Days 7-13 (4.5 mm at 168 hpf).
notes: No maxilla at 24, 48 or 120 hpf; the upper jaw is the palatoquadrate at those stages.

name: opercle
definition: Dermal bone that articulates anteriorly with the hyomandibula. The opercle is paired and typically the largest bone of the opercular series.  It is derived from the neural crest and is located in 2nd pharyngeal arch.

spatial.dv: lateral head wall behind the eye, covering the gill chamber
spatial.landmarks: dorsal apex articulates with the hyosymplectic; posterior free edge marks the head-trunk boundary and the anterior limit of the cleithrum

shape.notes: Fan: a rod at 3 dpf that widens into a fan by 4 to 5 dpf and a trapezoid in the adult. Keep the joint apex fixed and grow the ventral and posterior edges.

sizes.note: small linear spur at 3 dpf
fan shape emerges at 4 to 5 dpf
edge outgrowth 10.0 um/day (ventral) and 16.5 um/day (posterior) between 7 and 13 dpf
maxillary barbel reaches the middle of the opercle

events.event: opercle first mineralizes at 3 dpf as a linear spur
fan shape from 4 to 5 dpf
duck-like silhouette at about 13 dpf; growth 21.6 to 32.0 um/day between 13 and 19 dpf

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage Unknown. Kimmel et al. 2010 report first mineralization at 3 dpf.
notes: The opercular flap (ZFA:0000555) that covers the gills also contains the subopercle, interopercle and preopercle.

name: cleithrum
definition: Transversely oriented bone connecting the occipital region of the skull dorsally and pectoral girdle ventrally; appears near the end of embryogenesis.

spatial.dv: spans from the dorsal occipital region down to the ventral pectoral girdle, just behind the opercle
spatial.landmarks: posterior boundary of the head; the pectoral fin base sits on its ventral half

shape.notes: Curved dorsoventral splint, concave anteriorly, that thickens into a blade in the adult.

sizes.note: appears near the end of embryogenesis

events.event: ZFIN start stage High-pec
one of the earliest dermal bones with the opercle and branchiostegal ray 3 (3.4 mm NL)

notes: Direct ZFA part_of parent is the pectoral girdle ZFA:0000407, which is part of the pectoral fin skeleton.

name: vertebra
definition: All serially repeated ossified, cartilaginous, and ligamentous elements around the notochord (Schultze and Arratia, 1988).  Adult zebrafish usually 32 vertebrae but may have as few as 30 to as many as 33 vertebrae.

spatial.dv: axial midline around the notochord, ventral to the spinal cord and dorsal to the gut and swim bladder
spatial.landmarks: vertebra 1 follows the occiput; vertebrae 1-4 form the Weberian apparatus; 5-14 bear ribs; 15-29 are caudal; the last 3-4 are fused into the caudal fin complex

shape.notes: Array of 31 to 33 short cylinders (centra) with dorsal neural arches and, posterior to the vent, ventral hemal arches. Mineralization spreads anterior to posterior; drive centrum opacity by SL.

sizes.note: centra 3 and 4 mineralize at 4.0 mm TL; 5 then 1 and 2 by 4.4 mm TL
PU2 is the last centrum to form at 6.7 mm TL
about 22 mm of column in a 28 mm SL fish; 31-32 vertebrae per FishBase, mode 32 (30-33) per ZFA, mode 33 per Bensimon-Brito

events.event: ZFIN start stage Protruding-mouth for vertebra and centrum
first mineralized centra (3 and 4) at 4.0 mm TL, anterior-to-posterior
centrum 5, then 1 and 2, at 4.4 mm TL
caudal fin centra start with U1 of the compound centrum at 5.5 mm TL
PU2 is the last centrum, at 6.7 mm TL

notes: Direct ZFA part_of parent is vertebral column ZFA:0001559 (ZFIN start Unknown), which is part of the postcranial axial skeleton ZFA:0000317. Regions per Bensimon-Brito 2012: 4 Weberian, 10 abdominal, 15 caudal, 3-4 caudal fin vertebrae.

name: rib
definition: Endochondral bone that is intersegmental and rod-shaped, forming in the peritoneal membrane and attached to the vertebral parapophyses. Ribs protect and support internal organs.

spatial.dv: curve ventrolaterally from the parapophyses of the abdominal vertebrae around the body cavity
spatial.landmarks: on vertebrae 5 to 14 (non-Weberian precaudal vertebrae); enclose the swim bladder and gut

shape.notes: Ten pairs of thin curved rods, each about 40 to 60 percent of body depth, angled posteroventrally.

sizes.note: onset not verified; ribs are absent from the 5 dpf larva

events.event: ribs ossify after the centra during the late larval period (timing unverified; Bird and Mabee 2003 give the sequence)

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage Unknown. Rib onset is an estimate (about 6 to 7 mm SL); the ZFA lists ribs of vertebrae 1-6 as separate terms.

name: Weberian apparatus
definition: The Weberian apparatus consists of the modified anteriormost four vertebrae and associated structures of otophysans which transduce sound or pressure waves from the tunica externa of the swim bladder to the inner ear (Alexander, 1962).

spatial.dv: dorsal to the anterior chamber of the swim bladder, just behind the skull
spatial.landmarks: modified vertebrae 1 to 4 with the ossicle chain (claustrum, scaphium, intercalarium, tripus) linking swim bladder to inner ear

shape.notes: Four enlarged anterior centra plus a chain of three to four small paired ossicles on each side. At schematic scale, draw as a thickened anterior block of the column with a lateral bead chain.

sizes.note: ZFIN start Days 7-13; ossicles chondrify in larvae of 3 to 28 mm TL series

events.event: ZFIN start stage Days 7-13
tripus differentiates first, then intercalarium and scaphium; claustrum last (unverified order from Grande and Young 2004)
Weberian vertebrae 1-4 and post-Weberian supraneural ossify (ZFIN start Days 14-20 for supraneural)

notes: Bird and Mabee 2003 identify the Weberian apparatus as one of two separate centers of axial ossification (the other is the caudal fin).

name: hypural
definition: Expanded and laterally flattened hemal arches and spines. They support the lepidotrichia of the caudal fin. The hypurals form ventral to the posterior tip of the dorsally-flexed notochord. In zebrafish condensation of the hypurals begins at approximately 6 dpf (4.1 mm NL, notochord length).

spatial.dv: ventral to the upturned tip of the notochord (urostyle), inside the base of the caudal fin
spatial.landmarks: fan of 5 flattened plates below the urostyle; the diastema between hypural 2 and 3 marks the cleft of the homocercal fin

shape.notes: Five thin fan-shaped plates radiating posteroventrally from the notochord tip; hypural 1 and 2 below the diastema, 3 to 5 above. Appear in order 1, 2, 3 (days 4 to 6), 4 and 5 (days 7-13).

sizes.note: hypural 1 and 2 condensations (ZFIN start Day 4 and Day 5; 4.1 mm NL)

events.event: hypural 1 (ZFIN start Day 4); condensation of hypurals at about 6 dpf, 4.1 mm NL
hypural 2 (ZFIN start Day 5)
hypural 3 (ZFIN start Day 6)
hypural 4 and 5 (ZFIN start Days 7-13)
notochord flexion from 4.5 to 6.5 mm SL, final angle about 45 degrees

notes: Direct ZFA part_of parent is caudal fin skeleton ZFA:0000862 (ZFIN start Unknown), itself part of the caudal fin.

name: myotome
definition: Muscle that develops from somite and gives rise to body wall muscle masses.

spatial.dv: whole depth of the trunk and tail lateral to the notochord and spinal cord; epaxial half above and hypaxial half below the horizontal myoseptum
spatial.landmarks: myotome 1 follows the otic vesicle; 30 to 34 segments; each is a chevron pointing anteriorly at the horizontal myoseptum

shape.notes: Array of 30 chevron-shaped (later W-shaped) blocks per side. Segment length about 60 um at 24 to 48 hpf and about 700 um in a 28 mm SL adult. Nest a thin superficial slow layer over a deep fast core.

sizes.note: 59 um per myotome derived from the lateral line primordium speed of 100 um/hour = 1.7 myotomes/hour; height and width are estimates
3.9 mm larva
28 mm SL adult; one myomere per vertebra

events.event: first somite furrow (ZFIN start 1-4 somites)
somites form at 3 per hour for the first six, then 2 per hour
18 somites at 18 hpf
somitogenesis ends at about 24 hpf with 30 to 34 somites; tail somites are shorter
somite term ends (ZFIN end Pec-fin); the myotome persists to the adult

notes: Sub-regions with their own ZFA ids: epaxial myotome region ZFA:0001084 and hypaxial myotome region ZFA:0001085 (both 11.66 to 72 hpf in ZFIN).

name: horizontal myoseptum
definition: A connective tissue partition developing at the apex of the chevron-shaped myotome and separating dorsal (epaxial) and ventral (hypaxial) body wall muscle masses.

spatial.dv: horizontal plane at mid-depth of the myotome, at the level of the notochord
spatial.landmarks: the lateral line nerve and the lateral larval melanophore stripe run along it; the adult interstripe X0 forms over it

shape.notes: Thin horizontal sheet (connective tissue) that splits each myotome into epaxial and hypaxial halves; render as a 5 um seam.

events.event: ZFIN start stage 26+ somites
muscle pioneer slow cells that do not migrate mark the myoseptum position

name: slow muscle cell
definition: A muscle cell that is small, darkly colored, with high lipid and mitochondrial content.

spatial.dv: superficial monolayer on the lateral surface of each myotome in the embryo; a lateral wedge at the horizontal myoseptum in the adult
spatial.landmarks: directly under the skin, over the fast core

shape.notes: One-cell-thick red sheet (about 10 um) on the outer face of every myotome from 24 hpf. In the adult, replace by a triangular wedge along the horizontal myoseptum (superficial red muscle).

sizes.note: adaxial cells migrate radially to form a superficial layer
lateral red muscle wedge; dimensions unverified

events.event: ZFIN start stage 1-4 somites (adaxial cells)
adaxial cells migrate radially away from the notochord to become the superficial layer

notes: ZFA only has a cell-level term for slow muscle; used here as a tissue layer.

name: fast muscle cell
definition: A muscle cell that has a fast contractile response. Fast muscle fibers make up the deep portion of the myotome and are also known as white muscle cells.

spatial.dv: deep bulk of each myotome, medial to the slow layer, from the notochord to under the slow layer
spatial.landmarks: fills the chevron; multinucleate fibers span the whole segment

shape.notes: The same chevron blocks as the myotome minus the 10 um outer slow sheet. Pale pink.

events.event: ZFIN start stage 5-9 somites
lateral presomitic cells stay deep and differentiate into fast fibers

notes: ZFA only has a cell-level term for fast muscle; used here as a tissue block.

name: adductor mandibulae
definition: Is a mandibular muscle that forms along the palatoquadrates and inserts on Meckel's cartilages and functions in jaw closing.

spatial.dv: lateral to the palatoquadrate, behind and below the eye
spatial.landmarks: runs from the palatoquadrate/hyosymplectic to the posterior end of Meckel's cartilage; jaw closer

shape.notes: Short thick spindle (muscle belly) angled anteroventrally from the cheek to the jaw joint.

sizes.note: myoblasts differentiate in synchrony with the cartilage condensations
adductor mandibulae complex A1-A3 (ZFA:0000311)

events.event: ZFIN start stage High-pec
cartilage and muscle precursors of the arches differentiate up to 2 days before feeding at 4 dpf
ZFIN end stage Days 21-29; replaced by the adductor mandibulae complex term ZFA:0000311 from Days 30-44

notes: Direct ZFA relation is is_a mandibular muscle (ZFA:0000236); no part_of parent. UI parent set to the splanchnocranium so jaw muscles sit with the jaw.

name: sternohyoid
definition: Head muscle that originates on the anterior region of the cleithrum and inserts on the urohyal. The hypobranchial forms initially as left and right parts that later fuse together forming a cone shape.  The muscle is innervated by the occipitospinals and mainly composed of fast twitch muscle fibers.

spatial.dv: ventral midline of the throat, between the ceratohyals and the pectoral girdle, below the pharynx and heart
spatial.laterality: paired, fused to a midline cone
spatial.landmarks: from the anterior face of the cleithrum forward to the urohyal (behind the ceratohyal symphysis)

shape.notes: Cone with its base at the cleithra and apex at the urohyal; ventral surface of the head.

events.event: ZFIN start stage Long-pec; forms as left and right halves that fuse into a cone

notes: No ZFA part_of parent (is_a mandibular muscle). Companions on the ventral throat: intermandibularis ZFA:0000369, interhyoideus ZFA:0007051, hyohyoideus ZFA:0007052 (all 48 to 60 hpf).

name: pectoral fin musculature
definition: Musculature that is part of the pectoral fin.

spatial.dv: at the fin base on the ventrolateral body wall behind the opercle; abductor on the outer face, adductor on the inner face
spatial.landmarks: covers the endoskeletal disc / girdle at the fin base

shape.notes: Two flattened ellipsoids (abductor and adductor) at the base of each pectoral fin; scale with the fin base width.

sizes.note: ZFIN start Prim-25
discrete superficial and deep muscles from 7 mm body length; mature by about 12 mm TL

events.event: ZFIN start stage Prim-25 (primitive adductor at 36 hpf)
discrete superficial and deep fin muscles identifiable at 7 mm body length
mature muscle morphology established by about 12 mm total length

name: median fin fold
definition: Surface structure that will develop into one of the median fins.  Extends from dorsal surface of fish, caudal to the 8th somite, to the ventral surface ending at the caudal side of the  vent.

spatial.dv: continuous sagittal fold: dorsal from somite 8 back around the tail tip and forward on the ventral side to the vent
spatial.landmarks: dorsal fin fold ZFA:0000102 and ventral fin fold ZFA:0001069 are its two regions; the pre-anal part lies between vent and yolk extension

shape.notes: Thin translucent sheet (two epidermal layers around a mesenchyme-free space with actinotrichia) hugging the dorsal, caudal and ventral midline. Height about 5 to 8 percent of body length; taper toward somite 8 dorsally and the vent ventrally. Fade out by 144 hpf as the median fins condense.

sizes.note: barely present at the start of the pharyngula period; 1.9 mm embryo
prominent, with actinotrichia
3.9 mm larva

events.event: presumptive median fin fold (ZFIN 20-25 somites)
ZFIN start stage 26+ somites
barely present at the onset of the pharyngula period; becomes prominent and forms collagenous fin rays (actinotrichia)
ZFIN end stage Day 5; the fold persists as a remnant until the juvenile stage at 10.9 to 11.7 mm SL when fin fold loss is complete

notes: Actinotrichia (ZFA:0005435, ZFIN start Prim-5) are the unsegmented collagen rods that stiffen the fold. The fold gives rise to the dorsal, anal and caudal fins.

name: pectoral fin bud
definition: Fin bud that develops into the pectoral fin.

spatial.dv: lateral body wall at the yolk sac / trunk boundary, level with the horizontal myoseptum, just behind the otic vesicle and future opercle
spatial.landmarks: over somites 2 to 4; the bud points laterally then swings posteriorly

shape.notes: Low dome at 24 hpf, then an elongating paddle. Proximodistal length is 35 um at 30 hpf and 72 um at 46 hpf. Anteroposterior width is 116 to 135 um. Dorsoventral height is 85 to 79 um. Cap with a thin apical fold from 36 hpf.

sizes.note: bud forms at about 24 hpf; 30 hpf proximodistal length is 34.7 +/- 6 um
34.7 +/- 6 um proximodistal at 30 hpf; 116 +/- 10 um anteroposterior at 32 hpf
72.2 +/- 12 um proximodistal at 46 hpf; 135 +/- 12 um anteroposterior and 79 +/- 5 um dorsoventral at 44 hpf
elongated bud with a distal fold (Kimmel: Long-pec = elongated pectoral fin buds)

events.event: ZFIN start stage Prim-5; bud arises from lateral plate mesoderm by about 24 hpf
rudiments of pectoral fins are the staging landmark of High-pec (42 hpf)
elongated buds with central mesenchymal condensations that will form the girdle cartilage
ZFIN end stage Long-pec; the term pectoral fin (ZFA:0001161) continues

name: pectoral fin
definition: Paired fin that is located in the thoracic region of the body.

spatial.dv: ventrolateral, behind the opercle, above the yolk sac in the larva and low on the flank in the adult
spatial.landmarks: base on the cleithrum / scapulocoracoid; the larval fin points dorsoposteriorly, the adult fin lies against the flank

shape.notes: Paddle: an endoskeletal disc at the base plus a fan-shaped fold that becomes a rayed blade. Larval blade length about 2 to 3 times the base width. Adult: about 10 to 12 rays, 4 proximal radials and 6 to 8 distal radials, fin length about 0.15 to 0.2 SL.

sizes.note: ZFIN start Prim-15; bud proximodistal 34.7 um
bud 72 um at 46 hpf plus apical fold
pectoral fin blades (Kimmel Pec-fin stage)
about 8 percent of a 3.9 mm larva
0.18 SL in a 28 mm SL adult

events.event: ZFIN start stage Prim-15
fin blade expands from the apical fold (Pec-fin, 60 hpf)
endochondral disc formed proximal to the distal membrane by about 4 dpf
endoskeletal disc persists for about two weeks, then is remodeled into 4 proximal and 6 to 8 distal radials
adult fin morphology and muscle organization by about 12 mm TL; fin beat frequency falls from 28 Hz (larva) to 13 Hz (33 dpf juvenile)

notes: Pectoral fin ray count: the ZFA lepidotrichium definition gives about two more rays than distal radials. With 6 to 8 distal radials (Grandel and Schulte-Merker 1998) this gives 8 to 10 rays. Counts of 10 to 12 are common in the literature (unverified).

name: pelvic fin bud
definition: Fin bud that develops into the pelvic fin.

spatial.dv: ventral body wall, below the posterior lobe of the swim bladder, anterior to the vent
spatial.landmarks: small protuberances on the belly at 7.2 to 7.5 mm SL

shape.notes: Two low domes (about 100 um) on the ventral midline flanks; grow into short paddles before rays form at 8.5 mm SL.

sizes.note: PB stage 7.2 to 7.5 mm SL, about 3 weeks
before ray appearance at 8.5 to 8.7 mm SL

events.event: ZFIN start stage Days 14-20
pelvic fin bud appearance (PB) at 7.2 to 7.5 mm SL, about 3 weeks post fertilization
basipterygium cartilages present at 7.9 mm
ZFIN end stage Days 30-44; the pelvic fin term continues

name: pelvic fin
definition: Paired fin located in the abdominal position of the body.

spatial.dv: ventral, on the belly below the swim bladder, anterior to the vent and anal fin
spatial.landmarks: base on the basipterygium at about 0.5 SL; tip reaches toward the vent

shape.notes: Small triangular paired fin about 0.12 SL long. It has about 7 rays (unverified count). Rays appear at 8.5 to 8.7 mm SL and reach full number by 10 to 12 mm SL.

sizes.note: PR stage 8.5 to 8.7 mm SL
28 mm SL adult

name: dorsal fin
definition: Median fin that is located on the dorsal surface of the fish.

spatial.dv: dorsal midline, above the vent and anal fin origin
spatial.landmarks: single dorsal fin of about 10 rays on 8 pterygiophores (ZFA lists dorsal fin pterygiophores 1-8); origin slightly anterior to the anal fin origin

shape.notes: Triangular sail with a longer anterior edge; base about 0.12 SL, height about 0.12 SL in the adult. Condensation appears at 5.5 to 5.8 mm SL, rays at 6.4 to 6.6 mm SL.

sizes.note: DC condensation 5.5 to 5.8 mm SL
DR rays 6.4 to 6.6 mm SL; about 10 rays by 7.2 to 7.5 mm SL
28 mm SL adult

dorsal fin skeleton term starts (ZFIN Days 7-13)
dorsal fin condensation (DC) at 5.5 to 5.8 mm SL
dorsal fin rays appear (DR) at 6.4 to 6.6 mm SL; about 10 rays maximum

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage Unknown. Parichy et al. 2009 place the first dorsal fin condensation at 5.5 to 5.8 mm SL, which is about 14 to 17 dpf under their conditions (ZFIN stage table: 6.2 mm TL at 14 dpf).

name: anal fin
definition: Median fin that is located posterior to the anus.

spatial.dv: ventral midline, immediately posterior to the vent
spatial.landmarks: longer base than the dorsal fin; about 15 rays (10 to 12 branched); striped in the adult

shape.notes: Low triangular fin with a base of about 0.2 SL and height about 0.1 SL in the adult. Condensation at 5.2 to 5.5 mm SL, rays at 6.1 to 6.4 mm SL; all rays by about 8.5 mm SL.

sizes.note: AC condensation 5.2 to 5.5 mm SL
AR rays 6.1 to 6.4 mm SL
28 mm SL adult; branched anal rays 10-12

anal fin condensation (AC) at 5.2 to 5.5 mm SL
anal fin rays appear (AR) at 6.1 to 6.4 mm SL

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage Unknown. First condensation at 5.2 to 5.5 mm SL (Parichy et al. 2009), about 13 to 16 dpf.

name: caudal fin
definition: Fin that is the most posterior median fin. It is composed of a complex of three modified centra and modified neural and hemal arches and spines.

spatial.dv: posterior end of the body, centered on the axis; upper lobe above and lower lobe below the notochord tip
spatial.landmarks: the only fin present as a fold at 24 hpf; rays from 4.9 to 5.1 mm SL; homocercal forked fin with about 19 principal rays (ZFA principal rays 1-19) plus procurrent rays

shape.notes: Start as the rounded caudal end of the median fin fold. From 4.5 mm SL bend the notochord tip up 45 degrees. Grow a fan of about 19 to 20 rays below the tip. From 6.4 mm SL carve a middle cleft to make two equal lobes. Adult fork depth is about 0.05 SL and fin length about 0.2 SL.

sizes.note: posterior part of the fin fold around the tail tip
no rays yet; rays appear at 4.9 to 5.1 mm SL
about 20 rays by 6.0 mm SL; lobes emerge at 6.4 mm SL
28 mm SL adult; stripes extend onto the caudal rays

events.event: ZFIN start stage Prim-5 (as part of the fin fold)
notochord flexion begins at about 4.5 mm SL
caudal fin rays appear (CR) at 4.9 to 5.1 mm SL, about 16 dpf
nearly maximal ray number (about 20) by 6.0 mm SL; flexion complete by 6.5 mm SL with a 45 degree angle
dorsal and ventral lobes emerge at about 6.4 mm SL

name: lepidotrichium
definition: Dermal bone that is rod-like, formed and usually contained in a fin membrane, and jointed to or adjacent to distal radials. They are bilaterally paired.  Lepidotrichia are formed from paired hemitrichia surrounding actinotrichia. There are usually two more lepidotrichia than distal radials.

spatial.dv: inside every fin membrane, radiating from the fin base
spatial.landmarks: caudal about 19 principal rays; anal about 15; dorsal about 10; pectoral about 10 to 12; pelvic about 7 (pectoral and pelvic counts unverified)

shape.notes: Per fin, an array of tapered segmented rods (two hemitrichia each), branching distally in the branched rays. Segment length grows linearly with SL. Ray thickness about 20 um in juveniles, 80 to 100 um in adults.

sizes.note: caudal rays only
caudal plus anal plus dorsal rays
all fins

events.event: first caudal fin rays at 4.9 to 5.1 mm SL
anal fin rays 6.1 to 6.4 mm SL; dorsal fin rays 6.4 to 6.6 mm SL
pelvic fin rays 8.5 to 8.7 mm SL
ray segment addition proceeds linearly through about 11 mm SL

visibleFromNote: ZFIN start stage Unknown. First lepidotrichia (caudal) at 4.9 to 5.1 mm SL, about 16 dpf.
notes: Per-fin terms: caudal ZFA:0001550, dorsal ZFA:0001418, anal ZFA:0001421, pectoral ZFA:0001551, pelvic ZFA:0001552. All have ZFIN start Unknown. Lepidotrichia form around actinotrichia (ZFA:0005435).

name: periderm
definition: The outermost epidermal layer covering the fish at embryonic stages; derived from the EVL and thought to eventually be replaced by the superficial stratum of the epidermis. Sometimes used synonymously with EVL.

spatial.dv: outermost cell layer of the whole embryo including the yolk sac and fin fold
spatial.landmarks: derived from the enveloping layer (EVL, ZFA:0000086, 4.66 to 10 hpf)

shape.notes: Single squamous layer about 2 um thick over the whole body surface. Render it as the outer skin shell of the embryo from bud stage to 24 hpf. Then hand over to the epidermis term.

sizes.note: outer of the two epidermal layers
the two-layer epidermis is about 4 um thick at 24 hpf; the periderm is its outer layer

events.event: EVL forms as the outermost blastoderm monolayer (ZFIN start 30%-epiboly for EVL)
ZFIN start stage Bud for periderm
ZFIN end stage 26+ somites; the superficial stratum of the epidermis replaces it

name: epidermis
definition: A cellular, multilayered epithelium derived from the ectoderm. Zebrafish epidermis consists only of living cells unlike terrestrial vertebrates in which dead, keratinized cells are present.

spatial.dv: outer surface of the whole body and fins
spatial.landmarks: two cell layers until about 6 mm SL; stratifies to 4 to 6 layers by 8.6 mm SL

shape.notes: Body-hugging shell. Thickness is 4 um at 24 hpf. It stays two layers thick to about 25 dpf. It then grows about 4.7 um per mm SL. Adult thickness is 20 um on the head, 40 to 60 um on the dorsal trunk and 10 um on the ventral abdomen.

sizes.note: two cell layers, about 4 um
still two layers
two layers until about 20 dpf
20 um head, 40 to 60 um dorsal trunk, 10 um ventral abdomen

events.event: ZFIN start stage Prim-5; epidermis about 4 um, two layers
stratification begins at 5.4 to 6 mm SL (head) and 6.7 mm SL (dorsal trunk), about 25 dpf
four to six cell layers by 8.6 mm SL

notes: Strata with their own ZFA ids: epidermal superficial stratum ZFA:0001179 and basal stratum ZFA:0001180 (both from 10 hpf), intermediate stratum ZFA:0001181 (from Days 21-29).

name: dermis
definition: A collagenous layer of the skin subjacent to the epidermis and covering the hypodermis. It contains various types of cells (e.g. fibroblasts, pigment cells, nerve, blood vessels and scales.

spatial.dv: directly under the epidermis, over the hypodermis and muscle
spatial.landmarks: hosts the pigment cells, scales and the stratum compactum collagen layer

shape.notes: Thin collagenous layer under the epidermis. Collagen fibrils (22 nm) appear in an acellular subepidermal space at 24 hpf. The stratum compactum is 2 um at 7.5 mm SL and 5 um at 9 mm SL. Adult dermis is tens of um (estimate).

sizes.note: acellular collagen layer under the epidermis
orthogonal collagen plywood forms from 5 to 7 dpf
stratum compactum 5 um at 9 mm SL; adult value is an estimate

events.event: first collagen fibrils (22 nm) in the subepidermal space at 24 hpf; ZFIN start Prim-5
collagen plywood of the primary dermal stroma at 5 to 7 dpf
fibroblasts invade the dermal stroma at 20 to 26 dpf
scale primordia form in the dermis (ZFIN start Days 21-29)

notes: Hypodermis ZFA:0001136 (ZFIN start Days 14-20) lies under the dermis and also contains pigment cells.

name: scale
definition: Dermal bone that is thin, flexible, and platelike, and that develops in overlapping skinfolds that cover the body and often the head of fish and the bases of the fins.

spatial.dv: over the whole trunk and tail flank in overlapping rows; head is scaleless
spatial.landmarks: first row on the caudal peduncle, second row on the flank above the ribs; rows added dorsally and ventrally, columns anteriorly

shape.notes: Array of thin overlapping discs (elasmoid scales) in a hexagonal lattice; grow the lattice from the caudal peduncle forward over about 13 days. Adult scale diameter about 0.5 to 1 mm (estimate).

sizes.note: two rows within one day of onset; onset about 9 mm SL
count and diameter are estimates

events.event: scale primordium term starts (ZFIN Days 21-29)
scale development begins posteriorly over the tail at about 8.1 mm SL
squamation begins at about 9 mm SL; first row on the caudal peduncle, second row above the ribs; ZFIN start Days 30-44
squamation onset posterior (SP) 9.5 to 9.6 mm SL; through anterior (SA) 10.1 to 10.4 mm SL
full hexagonal coat after about 13 days; juvenile (J) 10.9 to 11.7 mm SL

notes: Stages 2R (two rows), 4R (four rows), B (beard, scales on dorsal anterior and post-mandibular skin) from Aman et al. 2018.

name: melanocyte
definition: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. Contains melanin-filled pigment granules, which gives a brown to black appearance.

spatial.dv: dermal and hypodermal pigment cells; in the embryo arranged in dorsal, lateral, ventral and yolk stripes; in the adult confined to the dark stripes
spatial.landmarks: first cells over the head and dorsal trunk at 24 hpf; also the retinal pigment epithelium (a separate ZFA term)

shape.notes: Point cloud of black stellate cells (about 30 to 60 um across). Render them as dark dots on the skin shell. Key density and stripe assignment to stage. Adult melanophores cover the 5 dark stripes.

sizes.note: early pigmentation is the Prim-5 landmark
four larval stripes forming
five dark stripes; counts are estimates

events.event: ZFIN start stage Prim-5; melanophores begin to differentiate at the onset of the pharyngula period
dorsal larval stripe (ZFIN Prim-15); retina pigmented
ventral larval stripe; tail pigmentation (Prim-25)
lateral larval stripe (High-pec)
yolk larval stripe (Protruding-mouth)
metamorphic melanophores appear at about 6.0 mm SL (MMA 5.9 to 6.3 mm SL)
adult stripes 1D and 1V discernible at about 9 mm SL

notes: ZFA name is melanocyte; synonym melanophore. Larval and adult stripe terms are separate entries in this file.

name: xanthophore
definition: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. Contains carotenoid pigments in structures called pterinosomes or xanthosomes. This gives an appearance ranging from a golden yellow to orange and red.

spatial.dv: scattered widely over the body in the larva; in the adult confined to the light interstripes over the iridophore sheet
spatial.landmarks: yellow cast over the dorsal head and trunk of the larva

shape.notes: Point cloud of yellow cells (about 40 um) on the skin shell; larval: diffuse dorsal; adult: dense in interstripes X0, X1D, X1V.

sizes.note: ZFIN start High-pec (42 hpf)
scattered widely over the body

events.event: ZFIN start stage High-pec
metamorphic xanthophores differentiate at about 6.5 mm SSL
xanthophores cover the iridophore sheet of the interstripes

name: iridophore
definition: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. The cell contains flat light-reflecting platelets, probably of guanine, in stacks called reflecting platets or iridisomes. The color-generating components produce a silver, gold, or iridescent color.

spatial.dv: eye and yolk sac in the embryo; dense sheet in the interstripes and a thin layer over the dark stripes in the adult; also the belly (argentum)
spatial.landmarks: first interstripe X0 forms at the horizontal myoseptum

shape.notes: Silver reflective patches. Embryo: an eye ring and yolk patches. From 4.5 to 4.9 mm SL: a horizontal band along the myoseptum (X0) that widens. Adult: dense sheets in all interstripes plus a silver belly.

sizes.note: ZFIN start High-pec; iridescent patches on the eye and yolk
dense sheets; count is an estimate

events.event: ZFIN start stage High-pec
metamorphic iridophores as early as 4.5 mm SSL; S-iridophores visible at CR stage (4.9 mm SL, about 16 dpf)
dense interstripe sheet X0 complete as stripes 1D and 1V form at about 9 mm SL

name: dorsal larval melanophore stripe
definition: A larval melanophore stripe that forms a band extending from the head to the tail along the dorsal apex of the myotomes.

spatial.dv: dorsal apex of the myotomes and the dorsal head, along the base of the dorsal fin fold
spatial.landmarks: from the head to the tail tip along the dorsal midline (paired left and right rows that merge over the head)

shape.notes: Thin band of melanophores along the named landmark. The band is one or two cells wide (about 40 to 60 um). Render it as a dark line or a strip of dots on the skin shell.

name: lateral larval melanophore stripe
definition: The larval melanophore stripe that is at the level of the horizontal myoseptum.

spatial.landmarks: along the horizontal myoseptum; the lateral line nerve runs with it

shape.notes: Thin band of melanophores along the named landmark. The band is one or two cells wide (about 40 to 60 um). Render it as a dark line or a strip of dots on the skin shell.

name: ventral larval melanophore stripe
definition: A larval melanophore stripe that forms a band, of pigmentation extending from the bases of the eyes on each side of the midline to the top of the tail, that underlies the myotomes bilaterally, still is dorsal to the yolk.

spatial.dv: ventral edge of the myotomes, dorsal to the yolk and gut, from the eye base to the tail
spatial.landmarks: paired band under the myotomes along the dorsal aorta level; passes over the yolk extension

shape.notes: Thin band of melanophores along the named landmark. The band is one or two cells wide (about 40 to 60 um). Render it as a dark line or a strip of dots on the skin shell.

name: yolk larval melanophore stripe
definition: The larval melanophore stripe that forms a band over the ventral surface of the yolk sac.

spatial.dv: ventral surface of the yolk sac and yolk extension
spatial.landmarks: band over the ventral yolk from the heart region back to the yolk extension tip; disappears with the yolk

shape.notes: Thin band of melanophores along the named landmark. The band is one or two cells wide (about 40 to 60 um). Render it as a dark line or a strip of dots on the skin shell.

name: melanophore stripe
definition: Surface structure composed of an array of melanophores arranged in a stripe.  Stripes are oriented from rostral to caudal.

spatial.dv: flank: stripes 1D and 1V flank the interstripe X0 at the horizontal myoseptum; 2D above and 2V below; stripes continue onto the anal and caudal fins
spatial.landmarks: X0 center sits at relative dorsoventral position 0.5 at 8 mm SL and 0.4 at 16 mm SL (unverified); five dark stripes and four light interstripes in the adult

shape.notes: Horizontal dark bands about 1 mm wide in a 28 mm adult. Lighter interstripes of equal width alternate with them. Order of appearance: 1D and 1V (9 mm SL), 2V (14 mm SL), 2D (16 mm SL), further stripes in large adults. Extend 1V and its neighbors onto the anal fin. Extend the central stripes onto the caudal fin.

sizes.note: 1D and 1V at about 9 mm SL
2V by 14 mm SL

name: barbel
definition: Surface structure which is a tactile structure found in the branchial region. Barbels are covered with epidermis rich in taste buds, and are innervated by branches of the cranial nerves.

spatial.dv: ventrolateral snout: maxillary barbel at the posteroventral corner of the maxilla (mouth corner); nasal barbel at the anterior nostril
spatial.landmarks: maxillary barbel reaches the middle of the opercle; rostral (nasal) barbel reaches the anterior orbit margin

shape.notes: Tapered whisker. It is 200 to 300 um wide at the base and 50 um at the tip. It is 2 to 4 mm long in 20 to 30 mm SL fish. It trails posteriorly along the cheek. There are two pairs (maxillary and nasal).

sizes.note: epithelial buds at 30 to 40 dpf, 10 to 12 mm SL
2 to 4 mm long, 200 to 300 um at the base, 50 um at the tip in 2 to 3 cm SL fish

ZFIN start stage Days 45-89 for barbel
barbel length correlates with standard length over a wide size range
